recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core source edit is needed for FHIR-11171 unless a future Patient Care decision changes either CarePlan.encounter or CarePlan.period semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-11171 was a Published/Not Persuasive with Modification Patient Care change request against DSTU2 CarePlan.context and CarePlan.duration. The accepted resolution said FHIR-11333 would clarify CarePlan.context as the original creation context and that there was no CarePlan.duration element, so CarePlan.period should clarify longitudinal care plan activities across encounters or episodes.
initial_application: The context portion was handled by FHIR-11333's application in commit f39dde8e171836d3345715f788c746e0a1624492. The period portion was applied in commit bd9f60dbffee762fd2b3e49ee2e07e232b9685a9, which changed the CarePlan.period comment to mention activities planned within a single encounter/episode or across multiple encounters/episodes, including longitudinal chronic-condition management.
additional_context: CarePlan is active in source/fhir.ini. Later workflow alignment renamed CarePlan.context to CarePlan.encounter and preserved the creation-context semantics in the current CarePlan.encounter definition and comment. The current CarePlan.period comment still contains the longitudinal-care wording requested by FHIR-11171. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active CarePlan source already contains both parts of the accepted resolution: CarePlan.encounter carries the clarified creation-context meaning, and CarePlan.period explains that scheduled activities may span a single encounter/episode or multiple encounters/episodes for longitudinal care.

related_jiras.note: The FHIR-11171 resolution explicitly relied on FHIR-11333 to clarify CarePlan.context as original creation context.
